# Samuccayakkhandhaka (Kd 13)

**ID:** Kd 13
**Section:** Khandhaka (kd)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Samuccayakkhandhaka
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The chapter on legal procedures in relation to offenses entailing suspension
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-kd13
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m3.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Samuccayakkhandhaka* is the thirteenth chapter of the Khandhaka in the Vinaya Piṭaka (situated as chapter 3 of the *Cullavagga*) [Frauwallner 1956; Norman 1983; SuttaCentral]. The text describes in extensive detail the canonical procedures for making amends when a monastic incurs an offense entailing initial and subsequent suspension (*saṅghādisesa*) [SuttaCentral]. It outlines the protocols for rehabilitation (*vuṭṭhānavidhi*), probation (*parivāsa*), and the six-day penance (*mānatta*) [Vinayamukha 1983]. Specific scenarios addressed include procedures when multiple monks incur suspension (such as when one conceals an infraction while another does not, requiring probation for the concealer before both are granted *mānatta* together) [Vinayamukha 1983]. It also preserves the formal transactional patterns (*kammavācā*) employed for rehabilitation, including an illustrative procedure enacted for Venerable Udāyi [Vinayamukha 1983], and deals recurrently with situations where a monastic disrobes (*vibbhamati*) and is subsequently permitted to re-ordain [Sujato 2009].

A notable textual feature is the concluding colophon to the chapter, which explicitly identifies the lineage of transmission: *ācariyānaṁ vibhajjavādānaṁ tambapaṇṇidīpapasādakānaṁ mahāvihāravāsinam vācanā saddhammatthitiyā* ("This is the recitation of the Vibhajyavādin teachers, who brought faith to the island of Tambapaṇṇi, the dwellers of the Mahāvihāra, for the preservation of the True Dhamma") [Skilling; Kang-yuan Sung 1999]. Scholars highlight this colophon as vital evidence for the redactional activity and final formalisation of the Theravāda Vinaya within the Mahāvihāra tradition of Sri Lanka [Skilling; Kang-yuan Sung 1999].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral identify the text with the *Pudgalavastu* of the Sanskrit Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya as well as the *Samuccaya* chapters extant in Tibetan and Chinese Vinayas (across the Sarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka traditions) [Prebish 1994; SuttaCentral]. Automated cross-language analysis by DharmaNexus likewise aligns the text with Sanskrit *Pudgalavastu* fragments and canonical Tibetan *Vinayavastu* texts [DharmaNexus]. Internally, DharmaNexus records extensive textual sharing with Vinaya commentaries such as the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā* and *Cūḷavagga-aṭṭhakathā*, along with canonical parallels in the *Samathakkhandhaka* (Kd 14) and the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* [DharmaNexus]. An English translation has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
